pressOrOkToEdit: Press ▼ or OK to edit settings.

warn.language: ⚠ Work in progress: only English is fully translated. Any other language leaves large parts of the game untranslated.
warn.cardCombat: ⚠ Replaces the standard battle scene. Turning this on turns Map Battle off.
warn.mapBattleMode: ⚠ Replaces the standard battle scene. Turning this on turns Card Combat off.
warn.markovLlmModel: ⚠ The model runs on the processor and wants a few gigabytes of memory. It writes English, and the first line of a session waits for the model to load.

desc.enemySpawnMode: How strong wandering enemies are. The year raises levels regardless: +10 a year to 2010, up to 110 in 2010-2011, nothing under 80 from 2012.
desc.weatherVolume: Volume of outdoor ambience: rain, storms, wind and biome sounds. Interiors are unaffected.
desc.biomeMusic: Let the place you stand in choose the music: each biome has its own tracks, one picked per country and per half of the day, with a darker set for an emptied world. Still being written, so it is off by default and every map keeps its own theme.
desc.partyHud: A card per party member in the top-left: HP, MP, states and urgent needs.
desc.musicArtistDisplay: Whether the game tells you what music is playing and who made it.
desc.battleMusicName: Which track plays when a fight starts. Biome, the default, uses the battle theme of the place you are fighting in. Random draws a different one of the tracks below at the start of every battle.
desc.markovLlmModel: Which GGUF language model writes generated dialogue. Off leaves every generated line to the Markov chains. Drop a .gguf file into the game's models folder and it is listed here.
desc.dialogueMode: How an NPC with nothing scripted to say responds when you talk to them. Empathize plays out a Socialize action from their personality, falling back to a flavour rumour. Markovian generates a fresh line from the NPC's own word bank instead.

enemySpawnMode: Biome: anything living here can appear. Seven spawns in ten are any level up to 110, all equally likely, so the place decides what you meet; the other three are pitched within five levels of your party, climbing with the year.
Party Level: enemies keep pace with your party. Roamers run from your own level up to ten above it; each tile hides one boss above that. The safest option.
Realistic: difficulty comes from the place, not from you. Levels rise the further a tile lies from where you started. Each nation and biome has its own roster, and every tile hides a boss.
Chaos: levels 1-110 roam anywhere, any biome. Procedural maps redeal their monsters on every entry.
musicArtistDisplay: First time: announced only the first time you hear a track. Changing this setting resets what it remembers.
Every time: a labelled tape slides in whenever the track returns. Never in battle, never twice within five minutes.
Minimal: track and artist in the usual corner notification.
